company.name: Twilio
company.shortDescription: Twilio is a cloud communication company that enables users to use standard web languages to build voice, VoIP, and SMS apps via a web API.
company.description: Twilio is a developer platform for communications and is reinventing telecom by merging the worlds of cloud computing, web services, and telecommunications. With Twilio, developers, and businesses make communications more contextual by embedding voice, video, messaging, and authentication directly into applications.

aiResearchSummary.text: Twilio is researching and developing systems for cloud-based communication, including a multi-tenant media processing platform for media intelligence, methods for searching and analyzing voice conversations, client communication in distributed telephony networks, real-time alerting for message delivery, multi-channel message exchange, and verifying incoming communications. These efforts focus on enhancing voice, VoIP, and SMS app capabilities via web APIs, message routing, and communication security.

insights.title: Funding is concentrated in the latest major round
insights.statement: The latest disclosed Post IPO Equity round raised $378,215,525, or 61.56% of reported total funding.
insights.implication: This round accounts for most reported historical financing, making it important when assessing funding-source concentration and fundraising cadence.
caveats: Crunchbase reports 11 rounds but provides 10 detailed rows.

insights.title: Valuation increased across disclosed rounds
insights.statement: Known post-money valuation rose from $500,000,000 to $1,000,000,000, a 2x increase.
insights.implication: The disclosed financing history indicates a material valuation step-up between the earliest and latest rounds with known valuations.
caveats: Only rounds with a disclosed post-money valuation are compared.

insights.title: Sharp recent attention and growth momentum
insights.statement: Crunchbase scores growth at 79 (-17 over 90 days) and market heat at 43 (-9).
insights.implication: The company has recently become much more visible, but the scores should be treated as attention/activity indicators rather than revenue or clinical-performance metrics.
caveats: Crunchbase does not expose the complete weighting behind these proprietary scores.
